The Gordian Empire and its four states

The Gordian Empire takes its name from Gordia, the northeastern state it was built around. The state names take Greek roots reshaped by a Germanic tongue (Arcaden, Delosen, Daedalen). The name plays on the Gordian knot: a society tied too tight to untie. This template comes from the formation of the German Empire. For now only the state names are changed, and everything else is kept as written. Former names are listed under each one.

Gordia

Northeastern state · template: Kingdom of Prussia

The largest and dominant state, centred on Berlin and stretching across northern and eastern Germany (plus the Rhineland and Westphalia). Culturally it was associated with the “Gordian virtues”: duty, discipline, order, punctuality, thrift and military efficiency. Predominantly Protestant (Lutheran in the core eastern and northern areas), though it included significant Catholic populations in the west. Society was more hierarchical and bureaucratic; the image was one of austerity, industriousness and reserve rather than exuberant festivity. Ethnically and linguistically diverse (including Polish-speaking areas in the east), it lacked a single folk culture and was often seen by southerners as stiff or authoritarian.

Stereotypical crimes
  • The paperwork murder: a ministry clerk's death is filed as suicide, with perfectly correct forms, because someone higher up needed it closed.
  • The duel that wasn't: officers settle honour by formal duel, and one death has all the right ceremony and the wrong wound.
  • Embezzlement in the chain ministry: money meant to maintain the anchor chains disappears, and a link fails.
  • The eastern minority: a Polish-speaking-style community on the far isles is blamed for everything, which makes it the perfect scapegoat.

Arcaden

Southern state · from Arcadia · template: Kingdom of Bavaria

The most culturally distinct southern state, with a strong sense of particularism and loyalty to the Wittelsbach dynasty. Predominantly Catholic (especially in the old heartland), it featured Alpine influences, elaborate Baroque churches, traditional costumes (Lederhosen and Dirndl), beer-garden culture and major festivals such as Oktoberfest. Arcaden dialects (part of the Upper German group) remain markedly different from northern German. The culture emphasised festivity, local traditions, rural life and a degree of resistance to Gordian centralisation; Munich served as a major cultural and artistic centre. Franconian and Swabian regions within the state added internal variety.

Stereotypical crimes
  • The festival killing: a death at the great autumn festival that everyone assumes was a drunken brawl, which is exactly what the killer is counting on.
  • The poacher feud: folklore makes the poacher a hero against the gamekeeper, and now a gamekeeper is found dead in the mountain woods.
  • Separatist chain-cutters: night saboteurs try to sever Arcaden from the web.
  • The stolen relic: a saint's relic vanishes from a Baroque church, and Protestant northerners get the blame.

Delosen

Mid state · from Delos · template: Kingdom of Saxony

A central/eastern state with a rich cultural and intellectual heritage. Strongly Protestant (Lutheran), it lay in the heartland of the Reformation. Dresden earned the nickname “Florence on the Elbe” for its Baroque architecture, art collections and courtly splendour, while Leipzig was a major centre of music (associated with Bach), trade and publishing. The Delosen dialect is distinctive. Delosen combined industrial and mining traditions (especially in the Ore Mountains) with a reputation for cultural refinement and a somewhat more easy-going or particularist character relative to Gordia.

Stereotypical crimes
  • The forged masterpiece: a painting or porcelain piece in the royal collection is fake, and the restorer who noticed is dead.
  • The printer silenced: a publisher is murdered the night before printing a pamphlet that would embarrass someone powerful.
  • The mine collapse: an accident in the ore mountains that is very convenient for an inheritance or an insurance claim.
  • Trade fair fraud: a merchant's ruin is engineered at the great market.

Daedalen

Southwest state · from Daedalus · template: Kingdom of Württemberg

A southwestern state centred on Stuttgart, associated with Swabian culture. Predominantly Protestant (Lutheran, with strong Pietist influences in the older core territories), though territorial expansions brought in Catholic areas in the south. Swabians have long been stereotyped for thrift, hard work, inventiveness, practicality and engineering skill (roots of the later automotive industry). The Swabian dialect belongs to the Alemannic group of Upper German. The culture emphasised diligence, local self-reliance and a solid, unflashy bourgeois ethos rather than courtly splendour or militarism.

Stereotypical crimes
  • The stolen patent: an inventor dies, and his rival files the design a week later.
  • The miser's will: a thrifty old man is poisoned for the savings everyone knew he was hiding.
  • The pious man's secret: a respected churchgoer is blackmailed over a hidden vice, and the blackmailer turns up dead.
  • Sabotage passed off as an accident: a machine, lift or chain mechanism is tampered with by someone who knows exactly how it works.

Delos

Bundesinsel · the central island where the four states meet

Named for the Greek island that was the meeting place and treasury of the Delian League. In myth it drifted freely until it was fixed in place. Here it sits at the centre of the chain web, and every state is moored to it.

Stereotypical crimes
  • Assassination at the assembly: a delegate dies mid-session, and all four states blame each other.
  • Bribery between delegations: votes are bought, and a bribe goes wrong.

The twist: each case opens by pointing at a cultural stereotype. The festival death looks like a drunken Arcaden brawl, and the stolen patent looks like Daedalen greed. Some cases confirm the stereotype and some defy it, so the player can never safely assume. Prejudice becomes part of the gameplay.

These regional identities—reinforced by religion (Protestant north/east vs. Catholic south), dialects, cuisine, festivals and monarchical traditions—meant that even under the Empire the four states felt culturally distinct, which helped justify their separate army contingents.

Main cast

Recurring characters. The Agent works for the Federal Chain and travels between the states; each state's local department has a point of contact who reappears whenever the Agent is in town. Type into any card to fill it in; changes save automatically.

Protagonist inspirations

Mood reference only, by another artist. We design our own detective in this spirit and don't copy the drawings. What we take from them: a static silhouette in one flat, cel-shaded block of colour, with only light, minimal line detail on top. The detective can live as that block, with a front, side and back orthographic view shown inside it.

The protagonist is left deliberately open. The player chooses which state the detective comes from and decides the rest for themselves.

Guiding philosophy

A bridge is never built and finished. Every bridge needs an engineer to maintain it, forever. Society and its comforts are the same: they are not a law of nature. They are kept up by a myriad of industries and professions, from engineers to law enforcement, so the status quo takes diligence.
Politics is personality. From how someone behaves and speaks, you can work out their connection to a crime.

Two endings

The chains cut both ways: they protect and they bind. Each ending takes one side of that to its limit. The game never says which is better.

Ending I

Severance

The chains are cut and the islands spread apart. Each one keeps its own identity, distinct from all the rest, but now it is cut off too. The epilogue tells us what each isle lacked without the help of the others.

Ending II

Absorption

An even larger landmass absorbs the rest: the vast, expanding power beyond the empire (a fantasy Russia), in the existential war still to come. This is the assimilation ending. The distinctions between the isles disappear as they conform to a single identity. Nothing is lost to the sky, and nothing stays its own.

Left ambiguous: it's up to the player's interpretation which ending is preferable.

Open questions

Answering these settles most of the map. Then we pick the first mechanic to build.

  1. What is the new school of magic?On the to-do list. What it does, who discovered it, and which guild it threatens most.
  2. One truth, or a verdict you choose?If the player names the culprit and can be wrong, the ripples become real consequences.
  3. What's the first case?The fire case is a clean tutorial: obvious evidence, one magic school, and a short list of suspects.
  4. Final titleThe working title is Chain State. Earlier working name: Project Chain Fels. “Chain” leads, standing for hierarchy, structure and authority. Gordia became the founding state and the Gordian Empire instead of the title. Still in play for the final name: Covenant, Pax, Harmonia, Mosaic.

Answered

  • What keeps the islands in the air? A war many years ago set the land in the sky. Nineteenth-century science can't study it, so people accept it as a fact of life. No other land can be found, and a mysterious landmass larger than the empire has been sighted.
  • Who gets to use magic? Guilds guard it as a secret and sell patented magic items, some of them everyday conveniences. Ordinary people don't know how it works and fear it. A newly discovered school is upsetting the established guilds.
  • What was the war that lifted the land? A war that is the nation's creation myth, the way the world wars shaped the modern world. It raised the land into the sky and separated it from the rest of the continent.
  • What is the landmass beyond the empire? A fantasy Russia. It isn't seen until the end of the game, but reports say it is far larger than all the isles together and aggressively expanding. It points to an existential war to come, which is where the assimilation ending lies.
  • How far can the Federal Chain be trusted? Deeply, like the Federation in Star Trek. Cases don't target the state itself unless the player pursues a separatist ending.
